finding.description: `put_many` writes to `self._data` without taking `self._lock`, while `get`, `put`, `invalidate` and the sweeper thread all mutate or iterate the same dict under that lock. A bulk insert that lands while the sweeper is walking `self._data.items()`, or while `put` is scanning for the oldest entry, raises `RuntimeError: dictionary changed size during iteration`; when it hits the sweeper thread, that thread dies and expired entries are never reclaimed.
finding.code_quote:
for key, value in items.items():
            self._data[key] = (value, deadline)

finding.description: `_evict_expired` deletes entries from `self._sessions` with no synchronisation, even though `create`, `get`, `revoke` and `revoke_user` all take the store's lock and sessions are touched from many request threads. A deletion that overlaps another thread's `get` or `create` can raise `RuntimeError` mid-iteration or drop a live session, so the eviction needs to run under the store's lock.
finding.code_quote:
for token in stale:
            del self._sessions[token]

finding.description: `first_error` reads `entry.level` straight after `parse_line`, which returns `None` for any line that does not match `LINE_RE` or carries an unknown level. A single stack-trace continuation or truncated write in the input raises `AttributeError: 'NoneType' object has no attribute 'level'` and aborts the scan before it reaches the first real error.

`owner` comes from `repo.get("owner")`, which is `None` for repositories whose owning account was deleted, so `owner["login"]` raises `TypeError: 'NoneType' object is not subscriptable`. Any such repo in the webhook payload crashes `resolve_team` instead of falling back to the default team.
finding.fix:
login = normalize_login((owner or {}).get("login", ""))
    team = TEAM_BY_LOGIN.get(login)

finding.description: `int(raw)` raises `ValueError` for any non-numeric amount such as `"12.50"` or `"abc"`, and `parse_amount` has no handler for it. A bad client payload therefore surfaces as an unhandled exception and a 500 rather than a validation error.

`flags & wanted == wanted` does not parse as `(flags & wanted) == wanted`: `==` binds tighter than `&`, so this evaluates `flags & (wanted == wanted)`, which is `flags & True` and only tests the lowest bit. Any token holding READ passes every `has_perm` check, including ADMIN and BILLING.
finding.fix: return (flags & wanted) == wanted

finding.description: `handle_download` joins the user-supplied `name` query parameter straight into the upload path. Unlike `save_upload` and `handle_delete`, which go through `_target` and strip directory components, this handler accepts `../` sequences and absolute paths, so an authenticated user can read any file the process can open, including other users' uploads.

"""Ad-hoc report queries over the orders table (sqlite3)."""
import sqlite3
from datetime import date

SORT_COLUMNS = {
    "created": "o.created_at",
    "total": "o.total_cents",
    "customer": "c.name",
    "status": "o.status",
}
DEFAULT_SORT = "o.created_at"
PAGE_SIZE = 50


def connect(path):
    conn = sqlite3.connect(path)
    conn.row_factory = sqlite3.Row
    return conn


def list_orders(conn, status=None, since=None, sort="created", descending=True, page=1):
    sort_col = SORT_COLUMNS.get(sort, DEFAULT_SORT)
    direction = "DESC" if descending else "ASC"

    clauses = []
    params = []
    if status:
        clauses.append("o.status = ?")
        params.append(status)
    if since:
        clauses.append("o.created_at >= ?")
        params.append(since.isoformat() if isinstance(since, date) else since)
    where = f"WHERE {' AND '.join(clauses)}" if clauses else ""

    sql = (
        "SELECT o.id, o.status, o.total_cents, o.created_at, c.name AS customer "
        "FROM orders o JOIN customers c ON c.id = o.customer_id "
        f"{where} ORDER BY {sort_col} {direction} LIMIT ? OFFSET ?"
    )
    params.extend([PAGE_SIZE, (page - 1) * PAGE_SIZE])
    return [dict(row) for row in conn.execute(sql, params)]


def revenue_by_day(conn, start, end):
    rows = conn.execute(
        "SELECT date(created_at) AS day, SUM(total_cents) AS cents "
        "FROM orders WHERE status = 'paid' AND created_at BETWEEN ? AND ? "
        "GROUP BY day ORDER BY day",
        (start, end),
    )
    return {r["day"]: r["cents"] for r in rows}

finding.description: The ORDER BY clause is built with an f-string that interpolates `sort_col` and `direction` directly into the SQL text. `sort` is a caller-supplied parameter, so a value such as `id; DROP TABLE orders` reaches the statement unescaped. Identifiers cannot be bound as parameters, which makes this an exploitable injection. Every value elsewhere in the module is bound with `?`, so this is the one place caller input shapes the statement.

`search` interpolates the caller-supplied `term` into the LIKE pattern with an f-string, so a search for `x%' OR role = 'admin' OR display_name LIKE '%x` is executed as SQL rather than matched as text and returns rows the term never matched. The other lookups in this class bind their values as parameters, which leaves this as the one query where user input reaches the statement text.
finding.code_quote: sql = f"SELECT {COLUMNS} FROM users WHERE display_name LIKE '%{term}%'"
finding.fix:
sql = f"SELECT {COLUMNS} FROM users WHERE display_name LIKE ?"
        args = [f"%{term}%"]

finding.description: `NamedTemporaryFile(..., delete=False)` leaves the file on disk after it is closed, and `write_snapshot` never removes it. Every export leaves another `.snapshot-*.tmp` file in the target directory, which slowly fills the volume; the `prune_orphans` helper at the bottom of the module exists only to mop up the same files.
finding.fix:
try:
        json.dump(payload, tmp, indent=indent, sort_keys=True)
        tmp.write("\n")
        tmp.flush()
        os.fsync(tmp.fileno())
        tmp.close()
        os.replace(tmp.name, path)
    finally:
        if os.path.exists(tmp.name):
            os.unlink(tmp.name)

finding.description: `collect_filters` uses a mutable default for `filters`. The list is created once at import time, and `build_query` calls the function without passing one, so each request appends its filters to the same shared list. Later requests inherit the filters of earlier ones and silently return the wrong rows.

The upper bound is off by one: `hi` starts at `len(events) - 1`, so the search interval stops short of the end of the list and the most recent event can never be returned by `last_at_or_before`. It should start at `len(events)`, the way `_lower_bound` does.
finding.fix: lo, hi = 0, len(events)

finding.description: The offset treats `number` as zero-based, but `parse_page` rejects `page < 1` and the module documents pages as 1-based. Page 1 therefore starts at row `size`, and the first `per_page` rows are never returned by any page.
finding.fix: offset = (number - 1) * size

finding.description: When retries run out on a retryable status, `call_with_retry` wraps a bare `RuntimeError` in `RetryExhausted`, so the caller loses the response object, its status code and any `Retry-After` header and can only recover them by parsing the message string. The last response should be kept on the exception.
finding.fix: last_exc = RetryableStatus(status, result)

finding.description: `forEach` ignores the promises returned by an async callback, so the handler never waits for `store.upsertItem`. The 201 response and the "import finished" log line are sent while the upserts are still running, and any rejection becomes an unhandled promise rejection that can terminate the Node process.

`documentIds.map(...)` produces an array of promises from an async callback, but nothing in the function awaits them. `enqueueReindex` can return before a single job has been added, so `queued` is computed from a still-empty `failed` list and reports success for jobs that later fail.

`mergeConfig` walks every own key of `source` with no filtering of `__proto__`, `constructor` or `prototype`. `JSON.parse('{"__proto__": {"admin": true}}')` creates an own `__proto__` property, so the recursion lands on `Object.prototype` and sets `admin` on every object in the process. `setPath` in the same file guards against exactly this, but the merge path does not.

`tryAcquire` checks `this.inflight` and increments it in two separate steps with no lock, so concurrent callers can both pass the `>=` test and push `inflight` above `limit`. This is a check-then-act race, and the limiter does not actually bound concurrency under load. Nothing in `acquire` or `release` compensates for the overshoot.

`listProjects` parses the response body without checking `res.ok`, unlike `getProject` and `archiveProject`. On a 401 or 500 the error body has no `projects` key, so the function returns `undefined` typed as `Project[]`, and `listActiveProjects` then throws `Cannot read properties of undefined (reading 'filter')` instead of an `ApiError` carrying the status.

The abort timer created here is never cleared when the request finishes first. Every call leaves a live `setTimeout` pending for `timeoutMs`, which keeps the Node process alive after the work is done and later calls `abort()` on a controller whose request already succeeded. There is no `clearTimeout` on the success path.

`scores.sort()` without a comparator orders numbers as strings, so `[9, 10, 100]` becomes `[10, 100, 9]` and `topScores` returns the wrong values once scores have different digit counts. It also sorts the caller's array in place.
finding.fix: const sorted = [...scores].sort((a, b) => b - a);

finding.description: The counter increment and the expiry are two separate Redis round trips. If the process dies or the connection drops between `INCR` and `EXPIRE`, the key is left without a TTL and the client stays throttled indefinitely. Make the pair atomic with a Lua script or `SET key 0 EX ttl NX` followed by `INCR`.
finding.code_quote:
const count = await redis.incr(key);
    if (count === 1) await redis.expire(key, windowSec);
finding.fix:
await redis.set(key, 0, "EX", windowSec, "NX");
    const count = await redis.incr(key);

finding.description: `defer f.Close()` inside the `for` loop does not run until `Build` returns, so every file in `paths` stays open for the whole run. With a few thousand paths this exhausts the process's file-descriptor limit and `os.Open` starts failing with `too many open files`.

`Deregister` deletes from `r.workers` without holding `r.mu`, while `Register`, `Heartbeat`, `Pick` and `Expire` all take it. A control-channel goroutine calling `Deregister` while the scheduler is inside `Pick` triggers `fatal error: concurrent map iteration and map write`, which takes the whole process down.

`cfg, err := readFile(path)` inside the `if` block declares a new `cfg` that shadows the one from the top of `Load`. The file's values are loaded into the inner copy and thrown away at the closing brace, so `Load` returns defaults plus environment overrides and silently ignores everything in `CONFIG_FILE`.

The response returned by `c.http.Do(req)` is never closed: nothing in `get` calls `resp.Body.Close()`, so each request leaks a connection from the transport's pool and the client stalls once idle connections run out.

`Add` assigns into `ix.docs` and `ix.postings`, both of which are nil on a zero-value `Index`. `var ix index.Index; ix.Add(d)` panics with `assignment to entry in nil map`. The maps have to be created in a constructor before the first write, and nothing in the file provides one.

`Put` acquires `c.mu` a second time before calling `evictOldest`, but the mutex is already held from the top of the method and `sync.Mutex` is not reentrant. The first insertion that pushes the list past `capacity` deadlocks the calling goroutine.

#!/usr/bin/env bash
# Build and package the release artifacts.
# Usage: build_release.sh [release|staging|debug]

MODE="${1:-release}"
ROOT="$(cd "$(dirname "$0")/.." && pwd)"
VERSION="$(git -C "$ROOT" describe --tags --always)"

log() { printf '[build] %s\n' "$*" >&2; }

case "$MODE" in
  release) BUILD_DIR="$ROOT/dist";         CFLAGS="-O2" ;;
  staging) BUILD_DIR="$ROOT/dist-staging"; CFLAGS="-O1 -g" ;;
  debug)   CFLAGS="-O0 -g" ;;
  *)
    echo "unknown mode: $MODE" >&2
    exit 2
    ;;
esac

log "mode=$MODE version=$VERSION"

if ! command -v make >/dev/null 2>&1; then
  echo "make is required" >&2
  exit 1
fi

log "cleaning previous build"
rm -rf "$BUILD_DIR"/*
mkdir -p "$BUILD_DIR"

log "compiling"
make -C "$ROOT" -j"$(nproc)" CFLAGS="$CFLAGS" OUT="$BUILD_DIR" || {
  echo "build failed" >&2
  exit 1
}

log "packaging"
tar -C "$BUILD_DIR" -czf "$BUILD_DIR/app-$VERSION.tar.gz" bin lib
sha256sum "$BUILD_DIR/app-$VERSION.tar.gz" > "$BUILD_DIR/app-$VERSION.sha256"
log "done: $BUILD_DIR/app-$VERSION.tar.gz"

finding.description: `rm -rf "$BUILD_DIR"/*` runs unconditionally, but `BUILD_DIR` is only assigned in the `release` and `staging` arms of the case statement. With `debug` the variable is empty, the glob expands to `/*`, and the script tries to delete everything the user is allowed to remove.

#!/usr/bin/env bash
# Rotate and compress application logs, keeping RETENTION_DAYS of history.
set -euo pipefail

LOG_DIR="${LOG_DIR:-/var/log/myapp}"
ARCHIVE_DIR="${ARCHIVE_DIR:-/var/log/myapp/archive}"
RETENTION_DAYS=14
DATE_STAMP="$(date +%Y%m%d)"

log() { printf '%s rotate_logs: %s\n' "$(date -Is)" "$*"; }

rotate_one() {
  local name="$1"
  local src="$LOG_DIR/$name"
  [ -s "$src" ] || return 0
  local dest="$ARCHIVE_DIR/${name%.log}-$DATE_STAMP.log"
  cp -p "$src" "$dest"
  : > "$src"
  gzip -f "$dest"
  log "rotated $name"
}

mkdir -p "$ARCHIVE_DIR"

cd "$LOG_DIR"
for f in *.log; do
  [ -e "$f" ] || continue
  rotate_one "$f"
done

cd "$ARCHIVE_DIR"
find . -maxdepth 1 -name '*.log.gz' -mtime +"$RETENTION_DAYS" -print -delete | while read -r old; do
  log "pruned $old"
done

log "rotation complete"

finding.description: If `cd "$ARCHIVE_DIR"` fails, the shell stays in `$LOG_DIR` and the following `find . ... -delete` removes `*.log.gz` files from the live log directory instead of the archive. The `cd` needs an explicit failure check before the destructive command runs.

finding.fix:
cd "$ARCHIVE_DIR" || exit 1
find . -maxdepth 1 -name '*.log.gz' -mtime +"$RETENTION_DAYS" -print -delete | while read -r old; do

#!/usr/bin/env bash
# Nightly Postgres backup: dump, compress, upload, prune old copies.
set -euo pipefail

BACKUP_DIR="${BACKUP_DIR:-/var/backups/pg}"
DB_NAME="${DB_NAME:?DB_NAME must be set}"
KEEP_COUNT="${KEEP_COUNT:-7}"
S3_BUCKET="${S3_BUCKET:-}"
STAMP="$(date -u +%Y%m%dT%H%M%SZ)"
OUT="$BACKUP_DIR/$DB_NAME-$STAMP.sql.gz"

log() { printf '[%s] %s\n' "$(date -u +%H:%M:%S)" "$*" >&2; }

dump() {
  log "dumping $DB_NAME"
  pg_dump --no-owner --format=plain "$DB_NAME" | gzip -9 > "$OUT.partial"
  mv "$OUT.partial" "$OUT"
}

upload() {
  if [ -z "$S3_BUCKET" ]; then
    log "S3_BUCKET not set, skipping upload"
    return 0
  fi
  aws s3 cp "$OUT" "s3://$S3_BUCKET/pg/$(basename "$OUT")" --only-show-errors
}

prune() {
  local count
  count="$(ls -1 "$BACKUP_DIR"/"$DB_NAME"-*.sql.gz | wc -l)"
  if [ "$count" -le "$KEEP_COUNT" ]; then
    return 0
  fi
  ls -1t "$BACKUP_DIR"/"$DB_NAME"-*.sql.gz | tail -n +"$((KEEP_COUNT + 1))" | xargs -r rm -f --
  log "pruned $((count - KEEP_COUNT)) old backups"
}

mkdir -p "$BACKUP_DIR"
dump
upload
prune
log "done: $OUT"

finding.description: `KEEP_COUNT` is assigned here and then never referenced, so the configured retention does nothing and dumps pile up in `BACKUP_DIR` until the disk fills. The script is missing a prune step that actually uses it, so a nightly run only ever grows the directory.
finding.fix: ls -1t "$BACKUP_DIR"/"$DB_NAME"-*.sql.gz | tail -n +"$((KEEP_COUNT + 1))" | xargs -r rm -f --

#!/usr/bin/env bash
set -euo pipefail

APP="${1:?usage: deploy.sh <app> <env>}"
ENVIRONMENT="${2:?usage: deploy.sh <app> <env>}"
REGISTRY="registry.internal.example.com"
IMAGE="$REGISTRY/$APP:$(git rev-parse --short HEAD)"
KUBE_CONTEXT="cluster-$ENVIRONMENT"

log() { printf '==> %s\n' "$*"; }

case "$ENVIRONMENT" in
  staging|production) ;;
  *) echo "environment must be staging or production" >&2; exit 2 ;;
esac

if [ "$ENVIRONMENT" = "production" ]; then
  branch="$(git rev-parse --abbrev-ref HEAD)"
  if [ "$branch" != "main" ]; then
    echo "production deploys must come from main (on $branch)" >&2
    exit 1
  fi
  if [ -n "$(git status --porcelain)" ]; then
    echo "working tree is dirty" >&2
    exit 1
  fi
fi

log "building $IMAGE"
docker build -t "$IMAGE" "apps/$APP"

log "pushing $IMAGE"
docker push "$IMAGE"

log "rolling out to $KUBE_CONTEXT"
kubectl --context "$KUBE_CONTEXT" set image "deployment/$APP" "$APP=$IMAGE"
kubectl --context "$KUBE_CONTEXT" rollout status "deployment/$APP" --timeout=300s

log "deployed $APP to $ENVIRONMENT"

finding.description: The rollout starts immediately after `docker push` with nothing confirming the push landed. If the registry rejects the image or the push is interrupted, `kubectl set image` still points the deployment at a tag that does not exist and the pods go into ImagePullBackOff. Verify the manifest with `docker manifest inspect` before rolling out.
finding.fix:
docker push "$IMAGE"
docker manifest inspect "$IMAGE" >/dev/null
kubectl --context "$KUBE_CONTEXT" set image "deployment/$APP" "$APP=$IMAGE"

-- stale_accounts.sql
-- Accounts that should receive the "we miss you" email and, after 180 days,
-- be flagged for deactivation. Run nightly by the lifecycle job.
--
-- accounts.last_login_at is NULL for accounts created through the invite flow
-- that never signed in; those must be included.

WITH recent_activity AS (
    SELECT account_id, MAX(occurred_at) AS last_event_at
    FROM account_events
    WHERE occurred_at >= now() - interval '365 days'
    GROUP BY account_id
),
open_invoices AS (
    SELECT account_id, COUNT(*) AS open_count
    FROM invoices
    WHERE status IN ('open', 'past_due')
    GROUP BY account_id
)
SELECT
    a.id,
    a.email,
    a.plan,
    a.created_at,
    a.last_login_at,
    r.last_event_at,
    COALESCE(oi.open_count, 0) AS open_invoices,
    CASE
        WHEN a.last_login_at < now() - interval '180 days' THEN 'deactivate_candidate'
        ELSE 'nudge'
    END AS action
FROM accounts a
LEFT JOIN recent_activity r ON r.account_id = a.id
LEFT JOIN open_invoices oi ON oi.account_id = a.id
WHERE a.deleted_at IS NULL
  AND a.plan <> 'enterprise'
  AND (
        a.last_login_at < now() - interval '60 days'
        OR a.last_login_at = NULL
      )
  AND COALESCE(oi.open_count, 0) = 0
ORDER BY a.last_login_at NULLS FIRST
LIMIT 5000;

finding.description: `a.last_login_at = NULL` never evaluates to true in SQL, because comparing anything to NULL yields NULL. Accounts that have never signed in are silently excluded from the nudge and deactivation lists, even though the header says they must be included. The predicate has to be `IS NULL`.
finding.code_quote:
a.last_login_at < now() - interval '60 days'
        OR a.last_login_at = NULL
finding.fix:
a.last_login_at < now() - interval '60 days'
        OR a.last_login_at IS NULL

-- customer_paid_totals.sql
-- Monthly report for finance: one row per active customer with the number and
-- value of PAID orders in the reporting window. Customers with no paid orders
-- must still appear with zeroes so the report reconciles with the CRM export.
--
-- Parameters: :month_start (date), :month_end (date, exclusive)

SELECT
    c.id                                   AS customer_id,
    c.name                                 AS customer_name,
    c.segment,
    COUNT(o.id)                            AS paid_orders,
    COALESCE(SUM(o.total_cents), 0)        AS paid_cents,
    COALESCE(SUM(o.refunded_cents), 0)     AS refunded_cents,
    MAX(o.created_at)                      AS last_paid_at
FROM customers c
LEFT JOIN orders o
       ON o.customer_id = c.id
      AND o.created_at >= :month_start
      AND o.created_at <  :month_end
WHERE c.status = 'active'
  AND o.status = 'paid'
GROUP BY c.id, c.name, c.segment
ORDER BY paid_cents DESC, c.name;

-- Reconciliation check: should return zero when run against the CRM export.
SELECT COUNT(*) AS missing_customers
FROM customers c
WHERE c.status = 'active'
  AND NOT EXISTS (
      SELECT 1 FROM crm_export x WHERE x.customer_id = c.id
  );

finding.description: The `o.status = 'paid'` predicate sits in the WHERE clause, which discards the NULL rows the LEFT JOIN produces for customers without matching orders. Customers with no paid orders in the window disappear from the report, turning the outer join into an inner join and breaking reconciliation with the CRM export.
finding.fix:
LEFT JOIN orders o
       ON o.customer_id = c.id
      AND o.status = 'paid'
      AND o.created_at >= :month_start
      AND o.created_at <  :month_end
WHERE c.status = 'active'

name: PR triage

on:
  pull_request_target:
    types: [opened, edited, reopened, synchronize]

permissions:
  contents: read
  pull-requests: write

concurrency:
  group: pr-triage-${{ github.event.pull_request.number }}
  cancel-in-progress: true

jobs:
  label:
    runs-on: ubuntu-latest
    timeout-minutes: 5
    steps:
      - name: Check out base branch (not the PR head)
        uses: actions/checkout@v4
        with:
          ref: ${{ github.event.pull_request.base.sha }}
          persist-credentials: false

      - name: Validate title format
        env:
          PR_TITLE: ${{ github.event.pull_request.title }}
          PR_AUTHOR: ${{ github.event.pull_request.user.login }}
        run: |
          echo "Checking title from $PR_AUTHOR"
          if ! printf '%s' "$PR_TITLE" | grep -Eq '^(feat|fix|docs|chore|refactor)(\([a-z0-9-]+\))?: .+'; then
            echo "::error::PR title must follow conventional commits"
            exit 1
          fi

      - name: Apply size label
        uses: actions/github-script@v7
        with:
          script: |
            const pr = context.payload.pull_request;
            const total = pr.additions + pr.deletions;
            const size = total < 50 ? "size/S" : total < 400 ? "size/M" : "size/L";
            await github.rest.issues.addLabels({
              owner: context.repo.owner,
              repo: context.repo.repo,
              issue_number: pr.number,
              labels: [size],
            });

finding.description: The PR title is attacker-controlled and it is expanded into the `run` script, so a title containing `$(...)` or backticks executes arbitrary commands on the runner. In a `pull_request_target` workflow that holds `pull-requests: write`, that is a direct script-injection path. Titles must never reach a shell unsanitised.

run: |
          echo "Checking title from $PR_AUTHOR"
          if ! printf '%s' "$PR_TITLE" | grep -Eq '^(feat|fix|docs|chore|refactor)(\([a-z0-9-]+\))?: .+'; then
